guide.title: Abdominal & Pelvic Trauma
guide.lead: The abdomen and pelvis hide large amounts of blood with few outside signs. Let the mechanism, the seat-belt sign and the vital signs guide you. Bind a broken pelvis, don't rock it, and get the patient to a surgeon.

steps.title: Suspect it
steps.text: High-energy mechanism, pelvic or groin pain, leg length difference, shock.

steps.title: Don't rock it
steps.text: No repeated springing of the pelvis.

steps.title: Bind it
steps.text: Pelvic binder centred on the greater trochanters (not the iliac crests).

steps.title: Permissive fluids, trauma centre
steps.text: Blood at the urethral opening: urethral injury – report it.

groups.title: Seat-belt sign
items: Bowel, mesenteric and lumbar spine injury

groups.title: Thoracoabdominal wound
items: Below the nipple line (front) or scapula tip (back): chest and abdomen

groups.title: Impaled object / evisceration
items: Moist dressing plus an occlusive layer; don't replace organs

groups.title: Pregnancy over 20 weeks
items: Any trauma: hospital and fetal monitoring

quiz.q: Seat-belt sign, distended abdomen, BP 96/60, HR 124, confused. Most likely?
quiz.explanation: Rigidity isn't needed for major bleeding.

quiz.q: Stab wound to the left lower chest at the anterior axillary line, absent breath sounds, hypotension. Suspect:
quiz.explanation: Below the nipple line can reach the abdomen.

quiz.q: 32 weeks pregnant, minor rear-end crash, no symptoms, normal vital signs. Management?
options: Transport for evaluation and fetal monitoring: abruption can follow minor trauma
quiz.explanation: Monitoring lasts several hours in hospital.

quiz.q: Crushed by a forklift: deformed pelvis, blood at the urethral opening, BP 78/50. Priority?
options: Pelvic binder at the greater trochanters, oxygen, permissive fluids, rapid transport
quiz.explanation: Blood at the urethra suggests urethral injury.

quiz.q: Where does a pelvic binder go?
quiz.explanation: The widest part of the pelvis.

options: It can disrupt clots and worsen bleeding

quiz.q: Kehr's sign suggests injury to the:

options: Moist sterile dressing plus an occlusive layer

flashcards.question: Solid vs hollow organ injury
flashcards.answer: Solid (liver, spleen, kidney, pancreas): bleeding and early shock. Hollow (bowel, stomach, bladder): leak and peritonitis over hours.

flashcards.question: Kehr's sign
flashcards.answer: Left shoulder pain from blood under the diaphragm: think spleen.

flashcards.question: Evisceration
flashcards.answer: Don't replace organs; moist sterile dressing plus an occlusive layer; transport.

flashcards.question: Why pelvic fractures kill
flashcards.answer: Large vessels and veins bleed into the retroperitoneum, which can hold several litres before tamponade.

flashcards.question: Pelvic binder position
flashcards.answer: Centred on the greater trochanters, not the iliac crests.

flashcards.question: Supine hypotension in pregnancy
flashcards.answer: After about 20 weeks the uterus compresses the vena cava when flat: manual left uterine displacement or tilt.

flashcards.question: Commonest cause of fetal death after trauma
flashcards.answer: Placental abruption: can follow minor trauma; bleeding may be concealed.

flashcards.question: Log rolls and pelvic fractures
flashcards.answer: Each roll can disrupt clots: bind first, use a scoop, minimise rolls.

critical.scenario: A worker fell onto rebar now impaled in his right lower abdomen; moderate bleeding around it. HR 124, BP 106/68. The foreman wants to pull it out.
critical.question: Management?

options.t: Stabilise the rebar with bulky dressings, don't remove it, oxygen to target, IV access en route, permissive fluids, trauma centre with pre-alert
Pull it out and apply pressure
options.f: It may be plugging the iliac vessels.

options.t: Pack tightly around it to push it in

critical.explanation: Early shock signs: watch closely en route.

critical.scenario: Unrestrained driver, head-on at about 80 km/h: severe lower abdominal and pelvic pain, seat-belt sign, left flank bruising, left leg shortened. HR 118. Still in the car.
critical.question: Suspected injuries and order of interventions?

options.t: Pelvic fracture, hip injury and abdominal bleeding: pelvic binder before extrication, splint the leg as found (no traction with a pelvic injury), scoop out with minimal movement, trauma centre

options.f: Traction is contraindicated with pelvic injury.

options.t: Spring the pelvis repeatedly to confirm

critical.kpi: Sequences pelvic binding and extrication in high-energy trauma

critical.scenario: 28 weeks pregnant, punched in the abdomen 30 minutes ago: firm, tender uterus, less fetal movement, fetal heart rate 174. No vaginal bleeding. HR 104.
critical.question: Likely complication and priority?

options.t: Placental abruption (bleeding can be concealed): manual left uterine displacement, oxygen, IV access, emergency transport to obstetric care, document the assault

options.f: A firm tender uterus after trauma is abruption until proven otherwise.

options.t: Lie her flat on her back

critical.explanation: Fetal tachycardia is an early distress sign. Consider safeguarding.
critical.kpi: Recognizes placental abruption after abdominal trauma in pregnancy
